neighbours.label: sentence-ending period or question mark in running prose, where more text follows
fire: My grandmother kept bees behind the barn for forty years. She sold the honey at the Saturday market in town.
The bridge was closed for repairs in early March. Commuters had to take the ferry across the river instead.
Have you ever wondered why the sky turns orange at dusk? The answer has to do with how light scatters in air.
The new policy took effect on the first of the month. Several managers said they had not been told about it.
In the experiment, the rats were given a sugar solution. Their activity levels rose sharply within an hour.
Our neighbour finally sold his old truck last week. He says he will buy a bicycle and ride it to work.
Is it really worth paying extra for organic apples? Many shoppers seem to think so, judging by the sales.
The museum reopened after a long renovation. Visitors can now see the dinosaur hall without a ticket.

notes: Card: 21 of the top 32 peaks are '.' or '?' closing a sentence that is followed by another. The + pole's output promotes 'but'/'However'; this pole sits on the boundary itself. Quiet items keep topic and length but are run-on clauses with no sentence-ending punctuation.
